title: Snail Mail
logline: The Puddleton Parcel Dash: the fastest couriers in town against one old snail with a letter to deliver. He can't outrun them, so he out-thinks them, with {product}.

world.setting: Puddleton, a fictional handmade clay town on a tabletop: sky-blue and silver cardboard houses, a hill street of painted card, a corrugated drainpipe running down the hill, cotton-wool clouds on wires, the Puddleton Parcel Dash street race from a chalk start line to the post-office mailbox at the bottom of the hill.
world.palette: Craft colours built from the can: sky-blue and silver card buildings, clay-red and gold accents (the start flag, the medal), cream paper road, green felt hedges.
fictional_brands: Puddleton Post (Gus's employer, green and cream satchel with a plain envelope shape, no letters)
Parcel Dash (the race, spoken only; its banners are blank bunting)
world.rules: Every banner, sign, mailbox and parcel is blank or a simple shape. The real can is the only real brand and the only non-handmade object on the set. Adult characters only.

beats.summary: The announcer pigeon does a double take: a snail is racing.
The start line, the flag drops, everyone blurs away; Gus has moved a thumb-width and is not worried.
At the refreshment stand the can towers over him; he sips through a long straw and his eyestalks snap sharp. The brand line.
He spots the drainpipe, tucks into his shell and rockets down the hill through the pipe.
He pops out at the mailbox and posts the letter first as the rabbit skids in behind him.
Gus on the bottle-cap podium with a medal, the can beside him. Tagline.

music.brief: Jaunty plucked banjo and woodblock in G major, 120 bpm, ragtime bounce, stops dead for the cork pop, then one lazy clarinet note for Gus.
Sparse: a soft ukulele vamp under the slurp, a bright xylophone run as his eyestalks snap straight.
The banjo theme at double time with brushed snare, tuba and a spiralling clarinet run down the drainpipe, a big brassy hit on the envelope going in.
The theme resolves on a warm banjo and tuba button, one final woodblock clop.
